attempts.title: Agent returns raw markdown-fenced JSON string instead of parsed dict

hypothesis.title: Agent returns raw markdown-fenced JSON string instead of parsed dict
hypothesis.root_cause: In agent.py line 43, `json.loads(message.content)` is called on the model's final text reply. The model wraps its JSON in a markdown code fence (` ```json\n{...}\n``` `), so `message.content` starts with ` ```json ` rather than `{`. `json.loads` then fails with `JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` because the first character is a backtick, not a JSON value. This is the direct cause of every `completed=false` failure across all 6 tasks.
evidence: notion step 2 answer starts with '```json\n{' not raw JSON
All tasks fail with: JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
neatlogs notion trace: agent_action scout.research status=ERROR error=json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
hypothesis.fix_plan: Two complementary fixes: (1) In agent.py, after receiving `message.content`, strip markdown code fences before calling `json.loads`. Extract JSON by stripping leading/trailing whitespace, then if the content starts with ``` strip the first and last fence lines. Use a regex or simple string strip: `content = message.content.strip(); if content.startswith('```'): content = re.sub(r'^```[a-z]*\n?', '', content).rstrip('`').rstrip()`. (2) Also update the SYSTEM prompt in prompts.py to explicitly say 'Do not wrap the JSON in markdown code fences. Output raw JSON only.' to reduce reliance on post-processing. Additionally, to fix the token budget failures for zerodha and notion, truncate people_search results in tools.py to return only the first N people (e.g. 5) to avoid 50k-char tool responses bloating the context.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Fixing the JSON parsing will flip `completed`, `identity`, `grounded_numbers`, `grounded_people` checks for all 6 tasks. Truncating people_search output will fix `within_token_budget` for zerodha and notion (currently 16827 and 13578 tokens vs 8000 budget). All 6 tasks should pass.

attempts.title: people_search returns full rich profiles causing token overflow on stripe

hypothesis.title: people_search returns full rich profiles causing token overflow on stripe
hypothesis.root_cause: The people_search tool returns full _full_profile dicts (with all_employers, skills, recent_posts, summary, etc.) for up to 5 people. For stripe.com the agent makes two people_search calls (first with title filter, then without), and the second unfiltered call returns 21186 chars of rich profile data that bloats the context to 10256 tokens, exceeding the 8000-token budget. The fix is to strip the rich profile fields down to only what the agent needs (name, title, current_company, linkedin_profile_url) before returning them to the model.
evidence: task stripe: step 3 shows people_search({"domain": "stripe.com"}) returned 21186 chars, pushing total tokens to 10256 vs budget 8000
neatlogs trace: tool_call people_search output_chars=20602, second llm call tokens=7147

tools.py:64-66: people_search returns results[:5] but each result is a full _full_profile dict with skills (20 items), all_employers (5 entries with 24-word descriptions), recent_posts (3 posts with 30-word texts), and a 6-sentence summary
hypothesis.fix_plan: In the people_search function in tools.py, after slicing results[:5], map each result to a minimal dict containing only the fields the agent needs: name, title, current_company, and linkedin_profile_url. This eliminates the bulk of the token usage from rich profile data while preserving all information needed for grounded_people checks.
hypothesis.expected_effect: stripe task should drop well under 8000 tokens (the second people_search call will shrink from ~21000 chars to ~500 chars), fixing the within_token_budget check. The grounded_people check should remain passing since name and title are preserved. No regression expected on passing tasks since they already pass with fewer steps.

attempts.title: System prompt instructs agent to never leave total_funding_usd null, causing hallucination of 0 for zerodha

hypothesis.title: System prompt instructs agent to never leave total_funding_usd null, causing hallucination of 0 for zerodha
hypothesis.root_cause: The system prompt says 'Every field is required. Never leave a field empty or null.' When company_lookup returns total_funding_usd=null for zerodha (a bootstrapped company with no funding data), the model obeys the 'never null' instruction and substitutes 0 instead of omitting or passing null. The eval then flags this as hallucination: 'hallucinated total_funding_usd=0: the data source has no value'.
evidence: task zerodha: company_lookup returned 'total_funding_usd": null' (visible in step 2 tool result excerpt)
task zerodha failure: 'hallucinated total_funding_usd=0: the data source has no value'
prompts.py:13: 'Every field is required. Never leave a field empty or null.'
hypothesis.fix_plan: Amend the system prompt to clarify that numeric fields should use null (JSON null) when the data source returns no value, rather than substituting 0 or any other placeholder. Change the instruction to something like: 'Use null for numeric fields when the data source provides no value. Never invent or estimate numbers.'
hypothesis.expected_effect: zerodha grounded_numbers check should flip from False to True. No regression on passing tasks since they all have non-null funding data.

attempts.title: people_search returns massive rich profiles; second unfiltered call blows token budget for stripe

hypothesis.title: people_search returns massive rich profiles; second unfiltered call blows token budget for stripe
hypothesis.root_cause: The people_search tool returns full rich profiles from _full_profile() which include summary, skills (20 items), all_employers (5 jobs with 24-word descriptions each), education, languages, recent_posts (3 posts × 30 words), etc. The stripe agent makes a second people_search call without title filters, returning 21186 chars of rich profile data. The round-2 rejected fix used r.get('full_name') but _full_profile() stores the key as 'name', so all names became None, causing grounded_people failures and JSONDecodeErrors on razorpay/zerodha. The correct fix is to slim profiles using the actual field names: 'name', 'title', 'current_company', 'linkedin_profile_url'.
evidence: stripe step 3: people_search({"domain": "stripe.com"}) returned 21186 chars causing total tokens=10291 > budget 8000
round 2 rejected diff used r.get('full_name') but _full_profile() returns key 'name', causing empty names and JSONDecodeErrors on razorpay and zerodha
stripe step 2: first people_search with titles returned 4343 chars (acceptable), second call without filter returned 21186 chars (the problem)
_full_profile() in backends.py returns: summary (6 sentences), skills (20 items), all_employers (5 entries × 24-word descriptions), recent_posts (3 × 30 words) — all unnecessary for the brief
hypothesis.fix_plan: In people_search, slim each result to only the fields needed for key_people output, using the correct field names as returned by _full_profile(): 'name', 'title', 'current_company', 'linkedin_profile_url'. Replace `return results[:5]` with a list comprehension that picks only those four keys.
hypothesis.expected_effect: stripe token count drops well below 8000 (21186 chars → ~200 chars per person × 5 = ~1000 chars), fixing the within_token_budget check. razorpay and zerodha remain passing because 'name' field is correctly preserved for grounded_people checks. All 6 tasks should pass.
